newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 18.

text.p: HOSPODASRSKE NOVINY - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party won the most support in the first round of the senatorial elections with 36.5 percent of the votes. The opposition Social Democrats were in second place with 20.3 percent of the votes.
- The senatorial elections saw surprisingly low voter turnout with only 35.03 percent of those eligible to vote actually casting their ballots.

- The elections will likely not have any noticeable effect on the country's economic situation. The Czech Republic is now in a situation where it does not make any difference how many seats a particular party wins, according to Helena Hessel, the manager of the international finance department of Standard and Poors.

- Representatives of 13 Central and Eastern European countries will meet in Prague today to discuss PHARE's transport program. The program has earmarked three billion crowns for these countries, 440 million crowns of which should go to the Czech Republic. The funds are to be used for investing in border crossings, training and pre-investment transport studies.

- CEZ a.s., the dominant Czech energy producer, posted a net profit of 7.037 billion crowns, an increase of 5.4 percent over the same period a year before. The company expects to post a net profit of 8.1 billion crowns at the end of the year, equal to last years profit.

- Apple Computer has a new representative on the Czech and Slovak markets. CDS, a member of the MDS group headquartered in Paris, is replacing TIS which recently broke its contract with the American computer company.
PRAVO - Ceska Sporitelna posted a net profit of 1.61 billion crowns in the first three quarters of 1996, according to Ceska Sporitelna's press spokesman, Pavel Jirousek.
